NiZn ferrite nanoparticles were synthesized using a self-combustion method with polyvinyl alcohol as a chelating agent.
Carbonyl iron and carbon black powders were milled for 12 hours at 300 rpm using grinding balls to obtain fine powders.
Three different weight ratios of Ni0.5Zn0.5Fe2O4/CI/CB composites were studied: 1:1:1, 1:1:2, and 2:1:1.
The composites were dispersed in a paraffin wax matrix with a weight ratio of 40% w/w.
The EMI shielding properties were measured in the frequency band of 8.8-12 GHz using the free-space technique.
The maximum shielding efficiency was 21.7 dB at 11.0 GHz for the 4 mm thick F/CI/CB-111 composite sample.
The multiple reflection loss can be ignored if the absorption shielding is higher than 10 dB.
The FTIR spectra confirmed the formation of metal-oxygen bonds in the NiZn ferrite and the presence of C=O and O-H functional groups.
The average particle sizes were 18-52 nm for NiZn ferrite, 0.2-2.4 μm for carbonyl iron, and 75-481 nm for carbon black.
The surface density of the prepared absorbers ranged from 3.62 to 4.04 kg/m^2.
Carbonyl iron was used to enhance the mechanism of magnetic loss, while carbon black was used to enhance the mechanism of dielectric loss.
The composites showed wide absorption bandwidths and reasonable surface density for EMI shielding applications.
The ternary composites of NiZn ferrite, carbonyl iron, and carbon black dispersed in paraffin wax were successfully synthesized.
X-ray diffraction, FTIR spectroscopy, and SEM analysis were used to characterize the composite materials.
The free-space technique was employed to measure the EMI shielding properties of the prepared samples.
